lessons.title: China and Hong Kong: Shanghai, Shenzhen, and the Hang Seng

children.text: In October 2024, foreign portfolio investors pulled a record ₹94,017 crore out of Indian equities in a single month. One big reason had nothing to do with India. Beijing had just unveiled a wave of economic stimulus, Chinese stocks were rocketing, and global funds sold expensive Indian shares to buy cheap Chinese ones. The trade even had a name: "Sell India, Buy China". A year later, Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index finished 2025 up 27.8%, its best year since 2017, and Hong Kong became the world's top IPO venue. Yet on 11 September 2026, the Shanghai Composite closed at about 3,887, still far below the 6,124 it reached in 2007. China's markets are huge, policy-driven and full of contradictions, and they directly affect money flowing into India.

body.text: "China" is really two stock markets: a mainland market of A-shares, dominated by domestic investors and shaped by capital controls and government policy, and Hong Kong, an open, dollar-linked gateway for global money. In both, policy moves prices more than almost anywhere else.

children.text: Mainland China's Three Exchanges

markDefs.definition: China Securities Regulatory Commission. Mainland China's securities regulator, broadly similar in role to SEBI but operating under much closer government direction.

children.text: Mainland China reopened stock exchanges in Shanghai and Shenzhen in 1990 as part of its market reforms, and added a third exchange in Beijing in 2021 for small and innovative companies. All three are regulated by the
CSRC
. Each exchange also runs special boards for technology and growth companies, with looser listing rules and wider daily price limits.

children.text: The Alphabet Soup of Chinese Shares

Chinese companies list in different places under different labels, depending on where they are incorporated and who is allowed to buy their shares. The same company can have two or even three listings. Learn these labels once and Chinese market news becomes much easier to follow.

cells: Mainland-incorporated companies listed in Hong Kong, priced in Hong Kong dollars
State-controlled companies with mainland businesses but incorporated outside the mainland
Privately owned Chinese companies incorporated offshore
Chinese companies listed in New York, often also in Hong Kong
An older foreign-currency class, now small and rarely traded

body.title: Name the share class
body.question: A company is incorporated in mainland China, already listed in Shenzhen, and raises money through a second listing on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange, priced in Hong Kong dollars. What are its Hong Kong-listed shares called?
body.explanation: Mainland-incorporated companies listed in Hong Kong issue H-shares. A company with both mainland and Hong Kong listings is called an "A+H" company. CATL did exactly this in May 2025, raising about $5.2 billion in Hong Kong including the over-allotment, the world's largest listing of that year. Red chips and P-chips are incorporated outside the mainland.

children.text: How the A-Share Market Works Differently

markDefs.definition: The trading links between Hong Kong and the Shanghai and Shenzhen exchanges. Northbound Connect lets investors in Hong Kong buy mainland A-shares; southbound Connect lets mainland investors buy Hong Kong stocks.

children.text: The mainland market is shaped by capital controls. The renminbi is not freely convertible, so foreign investors cannot simply open an account in Shanghai. Most foreign money enters through
Stock Connect

, launched between Shanghai and Hong Kong in 2014 and extended to Shenzhen in 2016, or through licensed institutional schemes. Domestic individual investors are a very large force in daily trading, which makes the market prone to sharp swings driven by sentiment and policy headlines.

body.title: A-shares vs Indian shares on NSE

columns.label: China A-shares
points: Shares bought today cannot be sold until the next trading day
Daily price limits of 10% on main boards and 20% on STAR Market and ChiNext
Foreign investors mostly access via Stock Connect or licensed schemes
State-backed funds often buy to support the market in sell-offs

columns.label: Indian shares on NSE
points: Intraday buying and selling on the same day is allowed
Price bands of 2% to 20% for non-F&O stocks; dynamic bands for F&O stocks
Foreign investors register as FPIs with SEBI
Rupee is convertible for trade and current account, with some capital account limits
No routine state intervention to support share prices

body.text: Policy risk is the defining feature of Chinese stocks. In 2015, a leverage-fuelled bubble burst and state-backed buyers stepped in. In January 2016, a new market-wide circuit breaker made panic worse and was scrapped within days. In November 2020, Ant Group's record IPO was halted days before listing, followed by a crackdown on technology platforms. A single policy announcement can move Chinese indices by 5% or more in a day, in either direction.

body.title: Growth without returns
body.prompt: The Shanghai Composite peaked at about 6,124 in October 2007. On 11 September 2026, it closed at about 3,887. What was the percentage change over that period? Enter a negative number for a fall, rounded to one decimal place.
body.explanation: Change = (3,887 ÷ 6,124 − 1) × 100 = (0.6347 − 1) × 100 = −36.5%. Over those 19 years, China's economy grew many times over, yet the index was still more than a third below its peak. Heavy new share issuance, state-owned companies that prioritise policy goals over shareholder returns, and a starting point of bubble valuations all contributed. Fast GDP growth does not guarantee good stock market returns, a lesson worth remembering when people argue that India's growth alone will carry the Nifty.

children.text: Hong Kong: The Gateway

markDefs.definition: Hong Kong's currency system, in place since 1983, which keeps the Hong Kong dollar trading within a narrow band of HK$7.75 to HK$7.85 per US dollar.

children.text: Hong Kong offers what the mainland does not: a freely convertible currency, an open capital account, a common law legal system and unrestricted access for global investors. Its currency is tied to the US dollar through the
Linked Exchange Rate System

, so Hong Kong interest rates broadly follow the US Federal Reserve. That makes Hong Kong the place where global money meets Chinese companies. After a painful slump from 2021 to 2024, Hong Kong came roaring back in 2025, helped by mainland investors buying through southbound Stock Connect, a technology rally and a wave of large A+H listings.

body.label: CATL's Hong Kong listing, May 2025
body.context: Including the over-allotment option. The Shenzhen-listed battery maker's secondary listing was the world's largest share offering of 2025, and A+H listings supplied more than half of Hong Kong's IPO fundraising that year.

children.text: The Hang Seng Index is Hong Kong's headline benchmark, weighted by free-float market cap with caps on the largest constituents. It is dominated by Chinese technology and consumer platforms such as Tencent, Alibaba, Xiaomi and Meituan, alongside financial giants like HSBC and AIA. The separate Hang Seng TECH Index tracks the 30 largest technology companies listed in Hong Kong. Because so many Hang Seng companies earn their money in mainland China, the index is a bet on the Chinese economy, priced in a currency linked to the US dollar.
The A-H Premium: Same Company, Two Prices

markDefs.definition: The extra price mainland investors pay for a company's A-shares compared with its H-shares in Hong Kong, after converting both into the same currency. The Hang Seng Stock Connect China AH Premium Index tracks it, with 100 meaning no premium.

children.text: An A+H company's two share classes carry the same rights to the same profits, yet they rarely trade at the same price. Mainland investors, who have limited overseas options, usually pay more for A-shares than global investors pay for H-shares. This
A-H premium

persists because capital controls stop investors from freely buying the cheaper shares and selling the dearer ones. On 29 April 2026, the AH Premium Index stood at 119.03, meaning A-shares traded at about a 19% premium on average.

body.caption: Convert the A-share price into Hong Kong dollars before comparing

body.title: Calculate an A-H premium
body.prompt: Illustrative figures: a Chinese bank's A-shares trade at 30 renminbi in Shanghai and its H-shares at HK$25 in Hong Kong. One renminbi equals HK$1.09. What is the A-H premium, in percent? Round to one decimal place.
body.explanation: A-share price in HK$ = 30 × 1.09 = HK$32.70. Premium = (32.70 ÷ 25 − 1) × 100 = (1.308 − 1) × 100 = 30.8%. Mainland investors are paying 30.8% more for exactly the same claim on the bank's profits. Remember a similar idea from Chapter 2: ADRs of Indian companies can also trade at a premium to their NSE price when moving shares between markets is restricted.

body.title: Hong Kong's closing bell
body.textWithBlank: Hong Kong's trading day ends at 4:00 pm Hong Kong time, which is ___ IST.
body.explanation: Hong Kong is 2 hours 30 minutes ahead of IST, so 4:00 pm HKT is 1:30 pm IST. That means Hong Kong's full trading day overlaps with NSE's morning session, and a big Hang Seng move can shape the Nifty's direction before lunch.

Large caps favoured by FPIs, such as HDFC Bank and Reliance
China is the world's biggest buyer of steel, copper and aluminium, so its property and infrastructure cycles move metal prices
Tata Steel, JSW Steel, Hindalco, Vedanta
Indian pharma, electronics and solar makers rely heavily on Chinese inputs
Pharma companies importing APIs, electronics manufacturers
Chinese overcapacity can push cheap goods into India
Steel, chemicals and solar equipment makers
Since 2020, India's Press Note 3 requires government approval for investment from countries sharing a land border, including China
Indian startups and companies seeking Chinese capital

body.title: A stimulus surprise from Beijing
body.scenario: At 7:45 am IST on a Wednesday, China announces a large package of property and consumption stimulus. By 9:00 am IST, the Hang Seng is up 5% and the Shanghai Composite is up 4%. Copper and steel prices are rising. GIFT Nifty is flat. You hold Tata Steel, Hindalco, HDFC Bank and a Nifty 50 index fund.
body.prompt: How might this news affect your holdings today and over the next few weeks? What lesson from October 2024 should you keep in mind?
body.modelAnswer:
Today:
1. Tata Steel and Hindalco are likely to rise. Chinese stimulus aimed at property and infrastructure lifts expectations for steel, copper and aluminium demand, pushing up metal prices.
2. HDFC Bank has no direct link to Chinese demand. Its move will depend more on Indian factors and FPI flows.
3. The Nifty 50 fund may see mixed effects: metals gain, while other sectors are largely unaffected on the day.

Over the next few weeks:
1. If Chinese stocks keep rallying, some emerging market funds may shift money from India to China, especially if Indian valuations look high. That could pressure FPI-heavy large caps such as HDFC Bank and weigh on the Nifty.
2. The October 2024 lesson: after Beijing's September 2024 stimulus, FPIs sold a record ₹94,017 crore of Indian equities in one month, and Indian indices fell about 8% from their peaks.
3. Chinese stimulus rallies have often faded when follow-through was weaker than hoped, so watch whether policy details and economic data confirm the initial excitement.

What to check: daily FPI flow data on NSDL, metal prices, the Hang Seng's trend over several days, and whether Indian earnings growth supports current valuations.

body.title: Your China and Hong Kong morning check
steps: At 7:00 am IST, note the opening moves in the Hang Seng and Shanghai Composite.
Check for any overnight policy announcements from Beijing, the PBoC or the CSRC.
Look at the Hang Seng TECH Index for the mood in Chinese technology stocks.
Check copper and iron ore prices if you hold Indian metal stocks.
Watch whether FPI flow data shows money rotating between India and China over several days, not just one.

body.title: China and Hong Kong Market Terms

cards.definition: Shares of mainland-incorporated companies traded in renminbi on the Shanghai, Shenzhen or Beijing exchanges.
Shares of mainland-incorporated companies listed in Hong Kong and traded in Hong Kong dollars.
The Shanghai Stock Exchange's science and technology board, launched in 2019, with 20% daily price limits.
Trading links between Hong Kong and mainland exchanges. Northbound lets global investors buy A-shares; southbound lets mainland investors buy Hong Kong stocks.
The extra price paid for A-shares over the same company's H-shares. The AH Premium Index was 119.03 on 29 April 2026.
Hong Kong's currency peg, keeping the Hong Kong dollar between HK$7.75 and HK$7.85 per US dollar.
The fund rotation after Beijing's September 2024 stimulus, which contributed to a record ₹94,017 crore FPI outflow from Indian equities in October 2024.

points: China has two stock markets: mainland A-shares on the Shanghai, Shenzhen and Beijing exchanges, and Hong Kong, an open gateway for global investors.
Chinese companies list under different labels: A-shares, H-shares, red chips, P-chips and US ADRs. A+H companies trade in both Shanghai or Shenzhen and Hong Kong.
A-shares cannot be sold on the day they are bought, face daily price limits of 10% or 20%, and are accessed by foreigners mainly through Stock Connect.
Policy is the biggest driver of Chinese stocks, from the 2015 crash to the 2020 tech crackdown and the September 2024 stimulus rally.
Fast GDP growth does not guarantee returns: the Shanghai Composite was still about 36.5% below its 2007 peak in September 2026.
Hong Kong rebounded strongly in 2025: the Hang Seng rose 27.8% and Hong Kong led global IPO fundraising with $36.0 billion, helped by A+H listings such as CATL.
China affects India through EM fund flows, metal prices, supply chains and competition. The "Sell India, Buy China" trade drove a record ₹94,017 crore FPI outflow in October 2024.
